about: Prism ML's Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B (Qwen3.8-27B architecture, ternary weights, thinking, tools) as the official Q2_0 packing with its built-in multi-token-prediction head, at the full 262,144-token window on one 24 GB card with everything on the GPU. Q2_0 is the packing that runs on stock llama.cpp; Prism's faster PTQ1_0 needs their fork and is not covered here. --spec-type draft-mtp drafts up to 3 tokens per step with Prism's suggested cut-off (n-min 0, p-min 0.1) and Bonsai verifies each one. q8_0 KV: only 16 of the 64 layers hold KV, so the full window takes about 9 GB. On an RTX 3090 that was also driving a desktop (about 1.1 GB) the whole card peaked at 20,738 of 24,576 MiB in a gate run, so about 3.8 GB stays free. On that machine the lab's speed gate read 95.6 tok/s with the draft and 69.1 tok/s with the four --spec flags removed; on short mixed answers the draft gained only 6 to 8% (median 74 to 76 against 69 to 70 tok/s). Text only: the repo's vision projector was not tested. llama.cpp from Unsloth's prebuilt b12588-mix-c0c3de8 (unslothai/llama.cpp, CUDA 13 portable), the build this was tested on. One slot, flash attention at its default, temperature 1.0, top-k 20, top-p 0.95, min-p 0 (the card's settings). Measured under WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04 on Windows 11), not bare-metal Linux.
setup: Not Docker; Linux x86-64 with an NVIDIA driver for CUDA 13. Unpack the archive into llama-b12588-mix-c0c3de8/ next to models/ and run from that directory. The archive does not bundle the CUDA runtime: put libcudart.so.13, libcublas.so.13 and libcublasLt.so.13 (PyPI nvidia-cuda-runtime 13.3.29 and nvidia-cublas 13.5.1.27) in cuda13-runtime/ and install libgomp1, or the server fails to load its CUDA backend.
